courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering with Laboratory
courses.description: Topics of special interest in mechanical and aerospace engineering with laboratory. May be repeated for credit as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Engineering Internship
courses.description: Students work in local industry or hospitals under faculty supervision. Units may not be applied toward graduation requirements. Salaried or unsalaried. Number of units determined by enrollment frequency. First quarter up to four units. Subsequent quarters cannot exceed one unit.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department stamp, 2.50 overall GPA minimum, at least ninety units.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular department curriculum, by special arrangement with a faculty member. May be taken P/NP only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Mechanics of Fluids
courses.description: This course covers topics in kinematics, equations of motion, dimensional analysis, laminar and irrotational flow, vorticity dynamics, and boundary layers.
courses.prerequisites_text: nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Thermal Processes
courses.description: This course covers topics in energy conservation, heat conduction, convection, radiation, heat transfer in ducts, external boundary layer, and heat exchangers.
courses.prerequisites_text: nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Solid Mechanics and Materials
courses.description: This course covers topics in kinematics, conservation laws, constitutive equation of linear elastic solids, plasticity, and viscoelasticity.
courses.prerequisites_text: nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Each graduate student in MAE is expected to attend one seminar per quarter, of his or her choice, dealing with current topics in fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, applied plasma physics and fusion, chemical engineering, applied ocean sciences, energy and combustion, environmental engineering, or materials science, and dynamics and controls. Topics will vary. (S/U grades only)

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Mathematics for Engineers
courses.description: This course will reintroduce the mathematics fundamentals necessary for success in the engineering graduate program in MAE. Topics will include calculus, ODE’s, vector calculus, linear algebra, probability and PDE’s.
courses.prerequisites_text: nongraduate students can enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics I
courses.description: Basic conservation laws. Flow kinematics. The Navier-Stokes equations and some of its exact solutions. Nondimensional parameters and different flow regimes, vorticity dynamics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Introduction to Gas Discharge Plasma Physics
courses.description: Charged particle motion in electromagnetic field, atomic processes in plasmas, electric breakdown of the gases, plasma quasi-neutrality, sheath, probes. Electron kinetics in low-temperature plasma, particle and energy fluxes, DC and RF driven discharges, instabilities of gas discharge plasmas.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Design and Control of Haptic Systems
courses.description: Course provides an introduction to the design and control of haptic systems, which provide touch feedback to human users interacting with virtual environments and teleoperated robots. Topics include haptic-focused mechatronic design, system modeling and analysis (kinematics and dynamics), human-in-the-loop feedback control, and haptic feedback evaluation. Course topics including mechatronic system design, as well as system modeling, analysis, and control reinforce many fundamental MAE topics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
courses.description: Fourier’s Law , the heat conduction equation, multidimensional conduction, unsteady conduction, moving boundary problems, conduction on slabs , cylindrical and spherical shells, multidimensional fins, numerical solution methods .
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Finite Element Methods in Solid Mechanics I
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SE 276A.) Finite element methods for linear problems in solid mechanics. Emphasis on the principle of virtual work, finite element stiffness matrices, various finite element formulations and their accuracy, and the numerical implementation required to solve problems in small strain, isotropic elasticity in solid mechanics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Computational Techniques in Finite Elements
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SE 233.) Practical application of the finite element method to problems in solid mechanics. Elements of theory are presented as needed. Covered are static and dynamic heat transfer and stress analysis. Basic processing, solution methods, and postprocessing are practiced with commercial finite element software. Students may not receive credit for SE 233 and MAE 235.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Electric Power Systems Modeling
courses.description: Formulate and solve canonical constrained optimization problems in electric power systems planning and operation, with applications to current and future low-carbon grids. Techno-economic assessment, implementations in a modern algebraic modeling language, and techniques to enhance computational tractability will be covered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Soft Robotics
courses.description: Roboticists have begun to explore the design of automated systems using soft materials (e.g., elastomers, gels, fluids) with the goal of achieving the versatility and robustness of biological organisms. This course provides a survey of topics important for the design, analysis, and control of soft robotics, including modeling (e.g., nonlinear elasticity), actuation (e.g., fluidic elastomer actuators), sensing (e.g., liquid metal sensors), and design optimization (e.g., using artificial evolution).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Structure and Analysis of Solids
courses.description: Cross-listed with NANO 227, MATS 227, and CHEM 222.) Key concepts in the atomic structure and bonding of solids such as metals, ceramics, and semiconductors. Symmetry operations, point groups, lattice types, space groups, simple and complex inorganic compounds, structure/property comparisons, structure determination with X-ray diffraction. Ionic, covalent, metallic bonding compared with physical properties. Atomic and molecular orbitals, bands vs. bonds, free electron theory. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: CHEM 222, MAE 251, MATS 227, or NANO 227.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Electronic and Photonic Properties of Materials
courses.description: (Cross-listed with MATS 251A.) The electronic and optical properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators. The concept of the band structure. Electronic and lattice conductivity. Type I and Type II superconductivity. Optical engineering using photonic band gap crystals in one-, two-, and three-dimensions. Current research frontiers. Students may not receive credit for MATS 251A and MAE 265A.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Linear Systems Theory
courses.description: Linear algebra: inner products, outer products, vector norms, matrix norms, least squares problems, Jordan forms, coordinate transformations, positive definite matrices, etc. Properties of linear dynamic systems described by ODEs: observability, controllability, detectability, stabilizability, trackability, optimality. Control systems design: state estimation, pole assignment, linear quadratic control.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Parametric Identification: Theory and Methods
courses.description: Constructing dynamical models from experimental data. Deterministic and stochastic discrete time signals. Discrete time systems. Nonparametric identification: correlation and spectral analysis. Parametric identification: realization and prediction error methods, least squares estimation, approximate modeling. Experiment design. Frequency domain identification. Recommended preparation: MAE 143C.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Hybrid Systems
courses.description: Definition of hybrid system. Examples in mechanics, vision, and multi-agent systems. Trajectories of hybrid systems. Chattering, Zeno phenomena. Stability analysis. Arbitrary switching: common Lyapunov functions. Slow switching: dwell time. State-dependent switching: multiple Lyapunov functions, Invariance Principle. Hybrid control design. Applications.
courses.prerequisites_text: MAE 281A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in numerical linear algebra. Fundamental matrix decompositions: LU, Cholesky, QR, Eigen, Schur, Jordan, SVD; how to compute them. Solution of large linear systems via iterative methods (Lanczos, Arnoldi, CG, GMRES). Stability of algorithms and conditioning of mathematical problems. Finite precision arithmetic and roundoff issues. Additional topics may include randomized methods for computing SVD/QR and solution of Lyapunov/Riccati equations for high-dimensional systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 203A.) Review of exact methods for ordinary differential equations. Expansions about regular and irregular singular points, eigenfunction methods for ordinary differential equations, special functions, Fourier series and integral transforms, linear algebra.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem as arranged by a designated faculty member. Must be taken for a letter grade only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in regular department curriculum, by special arrangement with a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing theses. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: First course of sequence in university reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students who have not completed a comparable course elsewhere. MCWP 40 introduces students to the basic elements of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Grades of C or higher are required for prerequisites. Students must take MCWP 40 for a letter grade to count toward the Muir College writing requirement. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 40, MCWP 40R, MCWP 40C, or MCWP 40CR.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Second course of sequence in reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students. MCWP 50 focuses on advanced skills of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Students will not receive credit for both MCWP 50 and MCWP 50R. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy the Muir College writing requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of the MCWP 40 requirement or completion of IGETC.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Argument and Analysis
courses.description: An advanced course in argumentation and analysis, with particular attention both to constructing arguments and analyzing the logic and rhetoric of others’ arguments. Students will engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. MCWP 125 courses are for transfer students who enter Muir College with TAG or IGETC. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 125, MCWP 125R, MCWP 50, or MCWP 50R. Course must be taken for letter grade to fulfill Muir College writing requirement.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Argument and Analysis
courses.description: An advanced course in argumentation and analysis, with particular attention both to constructing arguments and analyzing the logic and rhetoric of others’ arguments. Students will engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. MCWP 125 courses are for transfer students who enter Muir College with TAG or IGETC. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 125, MCWP 125R, MCWP 50, or MCWP 50R. Course must be taken for letter grade to fulfill Muir College writing requirement. This is a distance education course.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music A
courses.description: This course, first in a three-quarter sequence, is primarily intended for students without previous musical experience. It introduces music notation and basic music theory topics such as intervals, scales, keys, and chords, as well as basic rhythm skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Musicianship
courses.description: Primarily intended for music majors. Development of basic skills: perception and notation of pitch and temporal relationships. Introduction to functional harmony. Studies in melodic writing. Drills in sight singing, rhythmic reading, and dictation.
courses.prerequisites_text: passing score on proficiency exam or consent of instructor. Must be taken in sequence. Music majors must be concurrently enrolled in MUS 2AK, 2BK, and 2CK (Basic Keyboard).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Keyboard
courses.description: Scales, chords, harmonic progressions, transposition, and simple pieces.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 2A, B, C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Western Music
courses.description: A brief survey of the history of Western music from the Middle Ages to the present. Much attention will be paid to the direct experience of listening to music and attendance of concerts. Class consists of lectures, listening labs, and live performances.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music, Media, and Technology
courses.description: Exploration of the interactions among music, science, and technology, including the history and current development of science and technology from the perspective of music.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: American Music: Jazz Cultures
courses.description: Jazz is one of the primary foundations for American music in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. This course highlights the multicultural and international scope of jazz by taking a thematic rather than a chronological approach to the subject, and by highlighting the music and lives of a diverse array of jazz practitioners from around the country and around the world. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 8 and MUS 8GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. (Offered in selected years.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Popular Music
courses.description: A course on popular music from different time periods, covered through lectures, films, and listening sessions. Topics vary from year to year. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Instrumental/Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in instrumental technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in vocal technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Master Class
courses.description: All students enrolled in voice lessons (32V, 132V, or 132C) perform for one another and their instructors. Students critique in-class performances, with emphasis on presentation, diction, dramatic effect, vocal quality, and musicality.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 32V, 132V, or 132C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Composition I
courses.description: First course in a sequence for music majors and nonmajors pursuing an emphasis in composition. The course examines “sound” itself and various ways of building sounds into musical structures and develops skills in music notation. Students compose solo pieces in shorter forms. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 33 and 33A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2C or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music and music humanities majors every quarter a student is a declared music major. Four units or four quarters of enrollment are required of all undergraduate ICAM music majors who choose the MUS 43. Department Seminar option for their Visitor Series requirement. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit twelve times.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Practice I
courses.description: Study of modal counterpart in the style of the sixteenth century. Two-voice species counterpoint studies. Analysis of music of the period. Musicianship studies: sight-singing, dictation, and keyboard skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2C and 2CK.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Composition
courses.description: Advanced individual projects for senior music majors pursuing honors in composition. Projects will be critically reviewed in seminar with fellow students and faculty composers.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 103A-B-C and admission into the Department of Music Honors Program in composition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Critical Studies Seminar
courses.description: This seminar explores the history of music in relation to critical issues, such as race, gender, sexuality, the environment, and politics. Readings include recent literature in cultural studies, musicology, and sociology. Topics vary. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Restricted to music majors or consent of instructor; department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Classic, Romantic, and Modern Music
courses.description: This course will focus on topics in Western music from 1750 to the early twentieth century. May be taken for credit five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Department approval required. MUS 4, 8–10, or 120 recommended.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Popular Music Studies Seminar
courses.description: This course examines special topics in popular music from various sociopolitical, aesthetic, and performance perspectives. Readings include recent literature in cultural studies, musicology, and/or performance practice. Topics vary. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Music in Western Culture I
courses.description: This sequence introduces key concepts, histories, and practices in contemporary music studies. Students will explore methodological approaches and learn about current research through focused historical and ethnographic case studies.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 1C or 2C or passing grade on proficiency exam. Music majors are recommended to take MUS 101A concurrently. Department approval required for nonmajors.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Discover Jazz
courses.description: Offers an introduction to jazz, including important performers and their associated styles and techniques. Explores the often-provocative role jazz has played in American and global society, the diverse perceptions and arguments that have surrounded its production and reception, and how these have been inflected by issues of race, class, gender, and sexuality. Specific topics vary from year to year. (Cross-listed with ETHN 179.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Chamber Music Performance
courses.description: Instruction in the preparation of small group performances of representative instrumental and vocal chamber music literature. May be taken for credit six times, after which students must enroll for zero units.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music Performance
courses.description: Individual or master class instruction in advanced instrumental performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Recital Preparation
courses.description: Advanced instrumental/vocal preparation for senior music majors pursuing honors in performance. Repertoire for a solo recital will be developed under the direction of the appropriate instrumental/vocal faculty member. Special audition required during Welcome Week preceding fall quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: by audition only; MUS 132. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction in advanced vocal performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in the Vocal Master Class, MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Orchestra
courses.description: Repertoire is drawn from the classic symphonic literature of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries with a strong emphasis on recently composed and new music. Distinguished soloists, as well as The La Jolla Symphony Chorus, frequently appear with the orchestra. The La Jolla Symphony Orchestra performs two full-length programs each quarter, each program being performed twice. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Theory and Improvisation
courses.description: Study of jazz theory and improvisation, focused on fundamental rhythmic, harmonic, melodic, and formal aspects of modern jazz style. Application of theoretical knowledge to instruments and concepts will be reinforced through listening, transcription work, and composition and improvisation exercises. First course of a yearlong sequence.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2A-B-C, proficiency exam, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music majors every quarter.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz and the Music of the African Diaspora: Special Topics Seminar
courses.description: An in-depth writing and listening intensive investigation into a jazz or diaspora-related music history topic. Topics vary from year to year. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 126/ETHN 178, or MUS 127/ETHN 179, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Hip Hop: The Politics of Culture
courses.description: Examination of hip hop’s music, technology, lyrics, and its influence in graffiti, film, music video, fiction, advertising, gender, corporate investment, government, and censorship with a critical focus on race, gender, popular culture, and the politics of creative expression. (Cross-listed with ETHN 128.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Art of Sound
courses.description: Survey of applications of audio technology to music and related art forms. Physical and perceptual properties of sound and its artistic uses.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 1A, 2A, 5, 6, or 7, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Electronic Music Production and Composition
courses.description: Creative music production using digital audio workstations (DAWs), emphasizing hands-on composition projects including tempo warping, beat and tonality matching, virtual drum kits, chord progressions, sound processing and effects, arrangement, and remixing in the context of both popular and experimental genres. Existing works are analyzed and dissected for aesthetic value and production technique.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; restricted to music, ICAM-music, and ICAM-visual arts majors and minors, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Audio/MlDI Studio Techniques I
courses.description: First class in a yearlong sequence. Surveys hardware and software resources in an advanced analog/digital and media studio. Required course for use of the studio. Topics include: electronic and computer music, digital and analog audio signal mixing and manipulation, studio devices, interfacing, compositional applications, MIDI synchronization, performance and student projects. 174A focuses on signals, mics, device-based recording, mixing, monitoring.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 170; restricted to music, ICAM-music, and ICAM-visual arts majors and minors, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Concentrated inquiry into various problems not covered in the usual undergraduate courses.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department chair approval. Pass/Not Pass grade only.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading, research, or creative work under the direction of a faculty member, provided no course covering the material to be studied already exists, and the study area derives from previous course work.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department chair approval. Department approval required. Pass/Not Pass grade only. May be taken for credit twice.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Composition
courses.description: Meetings and laboratory sessions devoted to the study of composition in small groups. Consent of instructor required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Composition
courses.description: Meetings on group basis with faculty composer in sessions devoted to the study of composition.
courses.prerequisites_text: 203A-B-C and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Focus on Composition
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to bring in the entire population of the graduate composition program (all students and faculty) for in-depth discussion of critical issues in music theory and composition. Each meeting will feature a formal presentation by either a student, faculty member, or visitor, followed by lively and challenging debate on relevant issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Focus on Integrative Studies
courses.description: Meets on a biweekly basis to facilitate presentations by advanced students and invited guests and to encourage in-depth discussion between students, faculty, and visitors about theoretical and artistic issues of interest. Participation is required of all enrolled IS students until advanced to candidacy. Others are welcome to participate.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Experimental Studies Seminar
courses.description: Seminars growing out of current faculty interests. The approach tends to be speculative and includes individual projects or papers as well as assigned readings. In the past, such areas as new instrumental and vocal resources, mixed media, and compositional linguistics have been offered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Theoretical Studies Seminar
courses.description: Seminars on subject areas relating to the established dimensions of music and in which theoreticians have produced a substantial body of work. These include studies in analysis, timbre, rhythm, notation, and psychoacoustics. Offerings vary depending on faculty availability and interest. Analytical paper required.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music Performance
courses.description: Individual or master class instruction in advanced instrumental/vocal performance.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Orchestra
courses.description: Repertoire is drawn from the classic symphonic literature of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries with a strong emphasis on recently composed and new music. Distinguished soloists, as well as The La Jolla Symphony Chorus, frequently appear with the orchestra. The La Jolla Symphony Orchestra performs two full-length programs each quarter, each program being performed twice. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Focus on Performance
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to bring together performance students, faculty, and guests for discussion, presentation of student and faculty projects, performances by guest artists, and master classes with different members of the performance faculty.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (S/U grade option only.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Digital Audio Processing
courses.description: Digital techniques for analysis, synthesis, and processing of musical sounds. Sampling theory. Software synthesis techniques. Digital filter design. The short-time Fourier transform. Numerical accuracy considerations.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Survey of Electronic Music Techniques III
courses.description: A continuation of 271A and B, with emphasis on compositional techniques (e.g., computer-aided composition, production, spatialization).
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 271B and graduate standing in music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Research Methods
courses.description: Consideration and development of research methods appropriate to graduate-level scholarship and practice-based research.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (Letter grade option only.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research. (S/U grades permitted.) May be repeated for credit. Enrollment by consent of instructor only.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Research Projects and Independent Study
courses.description: Individual research projects relevant to the student’s selected area of graduate interest conducted in continuing relationship with a faculty adviser in preparation of the master’s thesis or doctoral dissertation.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Participation in the undergraduate teaching program is required of all graduate students at the equivalent of twenty-five percent time for three quarters (six units is required for all graduate students).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval. (S/U grade option only.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching—Nondepartmental
courses.description: Consideration and development of pedagogical methods appropriate to undergraduate teaching.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing and consent of instructor. (S/U grade option only.)

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Experience NanoEngineering
courses.description: Introduction to NanoEngineering lab-based skills. Hands-on training and experimentation with nanofabrication techniques, integration, and analytical tools. This class is for NANO majors who are incoming first-year students, to be taken their first year. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Engineering Computation Using MATLAB
courses.description: Introduction to the solution of engineering problems using computational methods. Formulating problem statements, selecting algorithms, writing computer programs, and analyzing output using MATLAB. Computational problems from NanoEngineering, chemical engineering, and materials science are introduced. The course requires no prior programming skills. Cross-listed with CENG 15. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: NANO 15, NANO 15R, CENG 15, or CENG 15R.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Introduction to Nanomaterials Synthesis Lab
courses.description: Lab-based course to introduce the chemical synthesis of nanomaterials. Hands-on training in chemical synthesis and basic characterization tools. Program or materials fees may apply.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Foundations in NanoEngineering: Chemical Principles
courses.description: Chemical and biochemical principles tailored to nanotechnologies. Chemical interactions, classical and statistical thermodynamics of small systems, diffusion, carbon-based nanomaterials, supramolecular chemistry, colloid and polymer chemistry, lipid vesicles, surface functionalization, catalysis, biomolecular interactions, and signal pathways. Priority enrollment given to NanoEngineering majors. Prerequisites : CHEM 6C. Restricted to NanoEngineering majors or by department approval.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Molecular Modeling of Nanoscale Systems
courses.description: Principles and applications of molecular modeling and simulations toward NanoEngineering. Topics covered include molecular mechanics, energy minimization, statistical mechanics, molecular dynamics simulations, and Monte Carlo simulations. Students will get hands-on training in running simulations and analyzing simulation results. Prerequisites : MATH 20F or MATH 18, NANO 102, NANO 104, and NANO 15 or CENG 15 or MAE 8. Restricted to NanoEngineering majors or by department approval.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Characterization of NanoEngineering Systems
courses.description: Fundamentals and hands-on practice of methods to image, measure, and analyze materials and devices that are structured on the nanometer scale. Optical and electron microscopy; scanning probe methods; photon, ion, and electron probe methods; spectroscopic, magnetic, electrochemical, and thermal methods.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 102.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: NanoEngineering System Design Seminar
courses.description: Seminar series focused on strategies in system design and solving engineering problems.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 115L.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: Fundamental laws of thermodynamics for simple substances; application to flow processes and to nonreacting mixtures; statistical thermodynamics of ideal gases and crystalline solids; chemical and materials thermodynamics; multiphase and multicomponent equilibria in reacting systems; electrochemistry.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Electrochemistry: Fundamentals and Applications
courses.description: Introduce fundamentals of electrochemical processes and electrode reactions to the principles of electrochemical techniques, instrumental requirements, and their diverse real-life applications in the energy, environmental, and diagnostics areas.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6A or 6AH, CHEM 6B or 6BH, CHEM 6C or 6CH, CHEM 7L or 7LM.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: NanoEngineering in Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to nanomedicine. Topics include nanoscale material, biological systems vs. synthetic vs. bio-inspired systems, drug and gene delivery, molecular imaging, vaccines, immunoengineering, pharmacology, clinical application in cancer, cardiovascular disease, infectious disease, immune diseases, genetic disorders, skin diseases, and regenerative medicine. Students will not receive credit for both NANO 175 and CENG 175.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Research project as equivalent to a “senior thesis” can be approved for two NanoEngineering elective courses (eight units total). This course is taken as an elective on a P/NP basis. It must be done in consecutive quarters and the student must find a faculty member who will oversee the research project. Eligible students must have completed at least ninety units and must have a UC San Diego cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better. Detailed policy and procedures may be obtained from the Student Affairs Office.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Chemical and Nano Engineering
courses.description: Each graduate student in chemical or nano engineering is expected to attend a weekly seminar dealing with current topics in nano and chemical engineering. Topics will vary. Cross-listed with CENG 205. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit up to four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Introduction to NanoEngineering
courses.description: Understanding nanotechnology, broad implications, miniaturization: scaling laws; nanoscale physics; types and properties of nanomaterials; nanomechanical oscillators, nano(bio)electronics, nanoscale heat transfer; fluids at the nanoscale; machinery cell; applications of nanotechnology and nanobiotechnology. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 201 and CENG 211.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Intermolecular and Surface Forces
courses.description: Development of quantitative understanding of the different intermolecular forces between atoms and molecules and how these forces give rise to interesting phenomena at the nanoscale, such as flocculation, wetting, self-assembly in biological (natural) and synthetic systems. Cross-listed with CENG 212. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 202 and CENG 212.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Structure and Analysis of Solids
courses.description: Key concepts in the atomic structure and bonding of solids such as metals, ceramics, and semiconductors. Symmetry operations, point groups, lattice types, space groups, simple and complex inorganic compounds, structure/property comparisons, structure determination with X-ray diffraction. Ionic, covalent, metallic bonding compared with physical properties. Atomic and molecular orbitals, bands verses bonds, free electron theory. Cross-listed with MATS 227, MAE 251 and CHEM 222. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: CHEM 222, MAE 251, MATS 227, or NANO 227.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing .

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Advanced BioPhotonics
courses.description: Basic physics and chemistry of interaction of photons with matter; photonic radiation pressure; advanced optoelectronic detection systems, devices, methods, time-resolved fluorescent, chemiluminescent methods, fluorescent energy transfer techniques, quantum dots, near-field optical techniques, mechanisms of light sensitive biological systems including chloroplasts for photosynthetic energy conversion and basis of vision processes. Cross-listed with BENG 247A and ECE 247A.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Quantitative basic understanding of different branches of polymer science varying from polymer chemistry, characterization, thermodynamics, rheological properties, smart materials, self-assembly in biopolymers (natural) and synthetic polymers, and applications of polymers ranging from medicine to structure. Cross-listed with MATS 257/BENG 242/MAE 257. Students may receive credit for one of the following: NANO 257, MATS 257, BENG 242, or MAE 257.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Quantum Mechanical Modeling of Materials and Nanostructures
courses.description: Application of quantum mechanical modeling methods (both solid state and computational chemistry) in the study of materials and nanostructures; density functional theory (DFT) and approximations; Hartree-Fock and beyond HF approximations; hybrid density functional theory; beyond DFT (GW, TDDFT); ab initio molecular dynamics; materials properties (mechanical, electrochemical, electronic, transport, nano-scale effects on properties) from quantum mechanical simulations; high-throughput computation.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Research in NanoEngineering
courses.description: Graduate research in NanoEngineering. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit four times for a maximum of twelve units. Prerequisites : consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Laboratory research under the supervision of individual members of the faculty of the neurosciences department in one or a combination of neurosciences disciplines, e.g., neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, neurochemistry, neuropharmacology. (P/NP grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Basic Neuroscience
courses.description: These courses are designed for graduate students in the neurosciences and other departments that are part of the interdisciplinary program (i.e., biology, cognitive science, psychology). These courses have been designed to cover as much basic neuroscience as possible in three quarters of study. It will combine two three-hour meetings each week with a 1.5 hour lecture and a 1.5 hour discussion of papers. These will be required courses for all first-year neurosciences graduate students. Biology will cross-list courses under biology headings, making it a requirement of first-year biology graduate students.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Ethics and Survival Skills in Academia
courses.description: This course will cover “ethical” issues in academia, including dishonesty, plagiarism, attribution, sexual misconduct, etc. We will also discuss “survival” issues, including job hunting, grant preparation, journal reviews, writing letters of recommendation, mentoring, etc. (W)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology
courses.description: Molecular and cellular approaches to the study of the nervous system are advancing neurobiology at an increasingly rapid pace. This graduate-level course will address the latest molecular advances in the areas of: 1) synapse formation, neurotransmitter release, and neurotransmitter receptors; 2) nerve growth factors, their receptors, and neuronal apoptosis; 3) transcriptional regulation in the brain and peripheral nervous system; 4) cell culture, transgenic, and knock-out mouse model systems; 5) the molecular bases of genetic, psychiatric, and degenerative diseases of the nervous system; and 6) the current molecular knowledge of vision, sensory transduction, circadian rhythms, learning, memory, and behavior.

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neuroscience Research Rounds
courses.description: Neurosciences group faculty members and graduate students will present and discuss ongoing research. Attendance will be mandatory for first- and second-year graduate students. Faculty, advanced graduate students, medical students, postdoctoral trainees, and other interested parties are encouraged to attend. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology General Clinical Selective Clerkship
courses.description: Provides opportunities for practical application of neurological skills to the understanding and treatment of a variety of clinical disorders of the nervous system.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of first two years of medical school. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Subintern Pediatric Neurology
courses.description: Subinterns are responsible for the primary care of hospitalized pediatric neurology patients under direct resident and attending physician supervision. Students will perform procedures such as lumbar puncture and participate in night call, daily teaching round, neurology grand rounds, and journal clubs.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurology 401 or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology Outpatient
courses.description: The student will rotate through the general and subspecialty (stroke, epilepsy, headache, nerve, and muscle) neurology clinics based at UC San Diego Medical Center, Perlman, VAMC, and Children’s Hospital. There are lectures and clinical conferences.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurosciences 401 or equivalent. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Clinical Independent Study
courses.description: Independent clinical study for medical students (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurosciences
courses.description: Specialized advanced topic areas in neurosciences will be addressed in an interactive seminar course format. A different specific topic will be considered each quarter as announced in advance. Students will each present an aspect of the topic area and participate in discussions.
courses.prerequisites_text: priority given to neuroscience PhD students, or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Tools for Experimental Data Analysis
courses.description: This course will cover a set of general data analysis methods that are broadly applicable in many different subdisciplines of psychology/neuroscience. Topics include model fitting, information theory, Fourier analysis, and machine learning. NEUG 231 is renumbered from NEU 231. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PSYC 231, NEUG 231, NEU 231. Recommended preparation: MATLAB, Python, C, Java, R, or any related language.

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Mathematical Foundations for Computational Neuroscience
courses.description: This course teaches mathematical concepts in neuroscience to students inexperienced in computation and mathematics. Topics from linear algebra, calculus, information theory, digital signal processing, graph theory, and machine learning will be covered. An optional weekly tutorial will teach computing basics. Priority enrollment is given to PhD students. MS students may enroll with instructor approval. Calculus AB is recommended but not required.

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Mechanisms of Pain
courses.description: Anatomical and pharmacological substrates activated following tissue or nerve injury will be discussed. Changes in afferents and spinal cord, including increased expressions of channels and receptors during chronic pain states will be emphasized. Clinical relevance and treatment will be included. (S/U grades only.) (F)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research Rotation
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Apprenticeship Teaching
courses.description: Participation in the department teaching program is required of all students working toward a PhD. In general, students are not expected to teach in the first year but are required to serve as teaching assistants or tutors for one quarter at any time during their subsequent years of training. The amount of teaching required is equivalent to the duties expected of a 50 percent assistant for one quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: neurosciences graduate students. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: SPPS
courses.title: Acute Care Adv Pharm Pract Exp

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: A general introduction to some of the fundamental questions, texts, and methods of philosophy. Multiple topics will be covered, and may include the existence of God, the nature of mind and body, free will, ethics and political philosophy, knowledge and skepticism. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Logic
courses.description: Basic concepts and techniques in both informal and formal logic and reasoning, including a discussion of argument, inference, proof, and common fallacies, and an introduction to the syntax, semantics, and proof method in sentential (propositional) logic. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Scientific Reasoning
courses.description: Strategies of scientific inquiry: how elementary logic, statistical inference, and experimental design are integrated to evaluate hypotheses in the natural and social sciences. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Ethics
courses.description: An inquiry into the nature of morality and its role in personal or social life by way of classical and/or contemporary works in ethics. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy: The Nature of Reality
courses.description: A survey of central issues and figures in the Western metaphysical tradition. Topics include the mind-body problem, freedom and determinism, personal identity, appearance and reality, and the existence of God. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.description: An examination of ethical principles (e.g., utilitarianism, individual rights, etc.) and their social and political applications to contemporary issues: abortion, environmental protection, and affirmative action. Ethical principles will also be applied to moral dilemmas in government, law, business, and the professions. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: CAT 2 and 3 or CAT 2CE and 3CE or CCE 1 and 2 or DOC 2 and 3 or HUM 1 and 2 or MCWP 40 and 50 or MCWP 40R and 50R or MMW 12 and 13 or WCWP 10A and B or SYN 1 and 2 or WARR 11A and 11B or SYN 1R and 2R.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society II
courses.description: An examination of a single set of major contemporary social, political, or economic issues (e.g., environmental ethics, international ethics) in light of ethical and moral principles and values. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 27 or POLI 27.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Ancient Philosophy
courses.description: A survey of classical Greek philosophy with an emphasis on Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, though some consideration may be given to Pre-Socratic and/or Hellenistic philosophers. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Living in a Digital World
courses.description: As our physical and digital lives increasingly merge, we face new challenges in understanding how to think about both worlds. This course will examine many philosophical issues and challenges that arise as our world rapidly becomes more digital. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy: Ancient
courses.description: An examination of ancient Greek philosophy, focusing on major works of Plato and Aristotle. PHIL 10, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Symbolic Logic I
courses.description: The syntax, semantics, and proof-theory of first order monadic and polyadic predicate logic. In this course, we will learn how to determine whether arguments that can be represented in first order predicate logic are deductively valid, how to symbolize English arguments, the rules of a natural deduction system, how to apply those rules to determine the logical status of symbolized arguments, and how to use semantic methods for determining validity and invalidity. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 10 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Metaphysics
courses.description: Central problems in metaphysics, such as free will and determinism, the mind-body problem, personal identity, causation, primary and secondary qualities, the nature of universals, necessity, and identity. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Moral Psychology
courses.description: The nature of action and psychological explanation. Topics include action individuation, reasons as causes, psychological laws, freedom and responsibility, weakness of will, self-deception, and the emotions. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology
courses.description: Philosophical problems in the biological sciences, such as the relation between biology and the physical sciences, the status and structure of evolutionary theory, and the role of biology in the social sciences. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and the Environment
courses.description: Investigation of ethical and epistemological questions concerning our relationship to the environment. Topics may include the value of nature, biodiversity, policy and science, and responsibility to future generations. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethical Theory
courses.description: Systematic and/or historical perspectives on central issues in ethical theory such as deontic, contractualist, and consequentialist conceptions of morality; rights and special obligations; the role of happiness and virtue in morality; moral conflict; ethical objectivity and relativism; and the rational authority of morality. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Technology and Human Values
courses.description: Philosophical issues involved in the development of modern science, the growth of technology, and control of the natural environment. The interaction of science and technology with human nature and political and moral ideals. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Feminism and Philosophy
courses.description: Philosophical examination of core concepts and theses in feminism, feminist philosophy, and critiques of traditional philosophical approaches to morality, politics, and science, from a feminist perspective. May also treat the historical development of feminist philosophy and its critiques. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in German Philosophy Translation—Advanced
courses.description: Continuation of PHIL 178 in the careful, line-by-line translation of passages of advanced difficulty from German philosophical texts, both classic (Kant, Fichte, Hegel, Schopenhauer) and contemporary (Heidegger, Wittgenstein, Habermas). May be repeated for credit three times with change of content .
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor or completion of PHIL 178.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Existentialism
courses.description: Classical texts and issues of existentialism. Authors studied will vary and may include Nietzsche, Kierkegaard, Heidegger, Sartre, de Beauvoir, and Fanon. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy Honors
courses.description: Independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, including a proposal for the honors essay. An IP grade will be awarded at the end of this quarter; a final grade will be given for both quarters at the end of 191B.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: The Honors Essay
courses.description: Continuation of 191A: independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, leading to the completion of the honors essay. A letter grade for both 191A and 191B will be given at the end of this quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Individual Study
courses.description: Directed individual study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.) May be repeated for credit four times with change of content and approval of instructor.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Proseminar
courses.description: Introduction to philosophical methods of analysis through study of classic historical or contemporary texts. Writing intensive. Enrollment limited to philosophy entering graduate students.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Core Course in Philosophy of Language
courses.description: An introduction to central topics in philosophy of language with emphasis on classic texts or contemporary authors. May be taken for credit three times with changed content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate status or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Science Studies: Part I
courses.description: Study and discussion of classic themes and texts in history of science, sociology of science, and philosophy of science, and of work that attempts to develop an interdisciplinary science studies approach. Required of all students in the Science Studies Program. Students may receive credit for one of the following: ANTH 268, COGR 225A, HIGR 238, PHIL 209A, or SOCG 255A.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Colloquium in Science Studies
courses.description: A forum for the presentation and discussion of research in progress in science studies by graduate students, faculty, and visitors. Students must attend the colloquium series for their entire first and second years. May be taken for credit two times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Metaphysics
courses.description: Topics may include identity, personal identity, universals and particulars, modality and possible worlds, causation, reduction, supervenience, freedom and determinism, space and time, and realism versus antirealism. May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.description: This seminar will cover current books and theoretical issues in the philosophy of science. May be taken for credit seven times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Agency, Morality, and Psychology Research Group
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on the topics of agency, morality, and psychology, and on contemporary research on these topics. The course is suitable for those specializing in moral psychology, agency, ethics, and philosophy mind and psychology, and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: German Philosophy Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets regularly to discuss primary or secondary literature in the area of German philosophy (including Kant, Fichte, Hegel, etc.). The reading is designed both for students doing active research in the field and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with it. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit twenty-one times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Phenomenology Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets biweekly with students reading and presenting material from the phenomenological literature. The course is designed both for students doing active research in phenomenology and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with that tradition. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Contemporary Philosophy
courses.description: Investigation of central issues in contemporary philosophy. Content varies but typically will center on a recent and important philosophical book. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science Topics and Methods
courses.description: This course meets weekly to discuss recent books or articles in philosophy of science. The reading is designed both for students doing active research in the field and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with it. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy Research and Methods
courses.description: This course meets to discuss work in progress in the history of philosophy. Its aim is to introduce understanding of the methods and standards of research in the field through constructive criticism of each other’s work. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Latin American Philosophy
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on Latin American philosophy. The course is suitable for those specializing in historical and contemporary philosophy in Latin America and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology Research Group
courses.description: A research group for graduate students engaged in philosophy or history of the biological sciences. The group discusses biological, historical, and philosophical articles and books and ongoing research projects. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Seminar on Special Topics
courses.description: Focused examination of specific problems or themes in some area of philosophy. May be taken for credit nine times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Physics Reading Group
courses.description: A research group for graduate students engaged in philosophy or history of the physical sciences. The group discusses physical, historical, and philosophical articles and books and ongoing research projects. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Greek Reading Group
courses.description: This group provides training in reading and translating philosophical Greek by having students prepare translations of passages and lead discussions. The group helps train graduate students preparing for Departmental Greek Exam. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Latin Reading Group
courses.description: This group provides training in reading and translating philosophical Latin by having students prepare translations of passages and lead discussions. The group helps train graduate students preparing for departmental Latin exam.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Supervised study of individually selected philosophical topics. S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Research Topics
courses.description: Advanced individual research studies under the direction of a member of the staff. Hours of outside preparation will vary with number of units taken. May be taken for credit nine times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: A course designed to satisfy the requirement that graduate students should serve as teaching assistants, either in the Department of Philosophy or in one of the writing programs offered by the various colleges. Each PhD candidate must teach the equivalent of quarter time for three academic quarters. Students are permitted to sign up as TAs for a maximum of eighteen quarters.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Professional Practice II
courses.description: The second in a series of four lecture-based courses dedicated to defining professionalism for healthcare providers. Lectures, readings, and discussion topics focused on patient- and family-centered care, understanding patients as people, working in interdisciplinary teams, and responding to adverse events.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Medicine I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture-based courses studying the clinical presentation, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of patients seeking care for common medical conditions in primary and specialty care settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapeutics I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture-based courses that explores the knowledge and concepts required to safely prescribe and monitor medications used to diagnose and treat common medical conditions in primary care and emergency department settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Human Physiology and Pathophysiology II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of two lecture-based courses that offers a comprehensive overview of normal human organ function, alterations in normal function, and the interaction of organ systems in states of health and disease.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Patient Education
courses.description: This course explores the effects of health literacy, patient education, and shared decision-making on patient care outcomes. Lab sessions will utilize clinical scenarios, case studies, and simulations that allow learners to practice new skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Reasoning I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture- and lab-based courses designed to engage learners in team-based activities that require them to integrate newly acquired knowledge and skill to develop and strengthen their clinical reasoning ability.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 212, PAE 215, and PAE 216.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Diagnostic Studies I
courses.description: The first of a two-part series designed to provide learners with an overview of common medical lab science assays utilized for the purposes of patient evaluation, diagnosis, and monitoring. Assay selection, interpretation, and value-based care concepts are emphasized.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics
courses.description: First quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course, geared toward life-science majors. Equilibrium and motion of particles in one and two dimensions in the framework of Newtonian mechanics, force laws (including gravity), energy, momentum, rotational motion, conservation laws, and fluids. Examples will be drawn from astronomy, biology, sports, and current events. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1A. Experiments in Mechanics. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1A and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. Electric fields, magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1B. Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, 1AL or 2BL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. The physics of oscillations and waves, vibrating strings and sound, and the interaction of light with matter as illustrated through optics and quantum mechanics. Examples from biology, sports, medicine, and current events. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1C. Experiments in waves, optics, and modern physics. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, 1BL or 2CL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Mechanics
courses.description: A calculus-based science-engineering general physics course covering vectors, motion in one and two dimensions, Newton’s first and second laws, work and energy, conservation of energy, linear momentum, collisions, rotational kinematics, rotational dynamics, equilibrium of rigid bodies, oscillations, gravitation. Students continuing to PHYS 2B/4B will also need MATH 20B. Students will not receive credit for both PHYS 2A and PHYS 2AR.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A-B or 20A or 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2A covering charge and matter, the electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, electromotive force and circuits, the magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, electromagnetic oscillations, alternating currents and Maxwell’s equations. Students continuing to PHYS 2C will also need MATH 20C or 31BH.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A and MATH 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20C or 31BH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Fluids, Waves, Thermodynamics, and Optics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2B covering fluid mechanics, waves in elastic media, sound waves, temperature, heat and the first law of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases, entropy and the second law of thermodynamics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, geometric optics, interference and diffraction. Students continuing to PHYS 2D will need MATH 20D.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and MATH 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20D. Prior completion of PHYS 2B is strongly recommended.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Experiments on L-R-C circuits; oscillations, resonance and damping, measurement of magnetic fields. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fee may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and 2B or 4C. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2C or 4D.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Relativity and Quantum Physics
courses.description: A modern physics course covering atomic view of matter, electricity and radiation, atomic models of Rutherford and Bohr, relativity, X-rays, wave and particle duality, matter waves, Schrödinger’s equation, atomic view of solids, natural radioactivity.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, 2B, and MATH 20D. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Modern Physics
courses.description: Experiments to be chosen from refraction, diffraction and interference of microwaves, Hall effect, thermal band gap, optical spectra, coherence of light, photoelectric effect, e/m ratio of particles, radioactive decays, and plasma physics. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2BL or 2CL . Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2D or 4E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 4B covering charge and Coulomb’s law, electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, AC circuits.
